{"metadata":{"description":"Structural code intelligence for DeepSeek Harness (dsh) — gives the agent codegraph and codegraph_index tools to find where a symbol is declared, what calls it, and what a change reaches, from a tree-sitter index it builds itself. Compatible with the codegraph CLI's on-disk forma","id":"gh:1336767699","install_available":false,"language":"TypeScript","name":"dsh-plugin-codegraph","slug":"CC19990113/dsh-plugin-codegraph","topics":["ai-agent","call-graph","code-graph","code-intelligence","codegraph","cordis","deepseek","deepseek-harness","dsh","dsh-plugin","llm-tools","static-analysis","tree-sitter"]},"paragraphs":[{"id":"p1s1","text":"Structural code intelligence for DeepSeek Harness (dsh) — gives the agent codegraph and codegraph_in"},{"id":"p1s2","text":"dex tools to find where a symbol is declared, what calls it, and what a change reaches, from a tree-"},{"id":"p1s3","text":"sitter index it builds itself. Compatible with the codegraph CLI's on-disk forma"},{"id":"p2s1","text":"# dsh-plugin-codegraph"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"English | 中文"},{"id":"p4s1","text":"Structural code intelligence for DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`)."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"Gives the agent two tools — `codegraph` and `codegraph_index` — so it can ask **where is this declar"},{"id":"p5s2","text":"ed**, **who calls it**, **what breaks if I change it**, and **how does one symbol reach another**, a"},{"id":"p5s3","text":"nswered from a pre-built index instead of from text search."},{"id":"p6s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p7s1","text":"## Why"},{"id":"p8s1","text":"An agent editing code asks structural questions before it touches anything. The tools it usually has"},{"id":"p8s2","text":" answer them badly or not at all:"},{"id":"p9s1","text":"- **grep** matches a name inside comments, strings, and unrelated identifiers, and cannot answer "wh"},{"id":"p9s2","text":"o calls this" at all.
- **LSP** answers precisely, but needs a running server per language, a warm w"},{"id":"p9s3","text":"orkspace index, and a *cursor position* rather than a name."},{"id":"p10s1","text":"A symbol graph answers all of it from one cheap lookup. This plugin ships both halves: a **store** t"},{"id":"p10s2","text":"hat serves queries from an on-disk graph, and an **indexer** that builds one, so a fresh workspace n"},{"id":"p10s3","text":"eeds no external tooling."},{"id":"p11s1","text":"## What the model gets"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"Two tools, deliberately separate."},{"id":"p13s1","text":"### `codegraph` — ten read-only operations"},{"id":"p14s1","text":"| Operation | Answers | Required |"},{"id":"p15s1","text":"| `search` | Where is a symbol declared? | `query` |
| `node` | One symbol with its immediate caller"},{"id":"p15s2","text":"s and callees | `symbol` |
| `callers` | What calls this? | `symbol` |
| `callees` | What does this "},{"id":"p15s3","text":"call? | `symbol` |
| `impact` | What can a change to this reach? | `symbol` |
| `trace` | How does o"},{"id":"p15s4","text":"ne symbol reach another? | `from`, `to` |
| `files` | What is indexed, under a directory or glob? | "},{"id":"p15s5","text":"— |
| `status` | How large and how fresh is the index? | — |
| `explore` | Several related declarati"},{"id":"p15s6","text":"ons with their source | `query` |
| `context` | Everything relevant to a task | `task` |"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"The tool also reports its own state into the system prompt. Every prompt assembly carries one line d"},{"id":"p16s2","text":"escribing the workspace's index — how many files, declarations and relationships it holds, when it w"},{"id":"p16s3","text":"as built, and how many generated artifacts were left out — or, when there is none, that `codegraph_i"},{"id":"p16s4","text":"ndex` has to run first. That line is a section whose text is a function, re-evaluated per request by"},{"id":"p16s5","text":" the host; nothing is spent on a `status` round-trip to learn it."},{"id":"p17s1","text":"**Re-indexing parses only what changed.** Every successful run leaves the extraction it produced for"},{"id":"p17s2","text":" each file in `.codegraph/cache/`; the next run — a second `codegraph_index`, or a watch rebuild aft"},{"id":"p17s3","text":"er one edit — confirms each file by its recorded modification time and size and reuses its extractio"},{"id":"p17s4","text":"n instead of reading and parsing it again. On a 337-file workspace measured here, a repeat run cost "},{"id":"p17s5","text":"45 ms against 991 ms for the first. Edges and call resolution are still rebuilt over the whole graph"},{"id":"p17s6","text":" every time, deliberately: the rule that resolves a call by a workspace-unique name is global, so a "},{"id":"p17s7","text":"symbol added in one file can invalidate edges pointing at another that never changed. `cacheVerify: "},{"id":"p17s8","text":"'hash'` trades that speed for correctness when a checkout can restore an older file without moving i"},{"id":"p17s9","text":"rades that speed for correctness when a checkout can restore an older file without moving its mtime."},{"id":"p18s1","text":"[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p19s1","text":"### `codegraph_index` — build or refresh the graph"},{"id":"p20s1","text":"[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p21s1","text":"## Interoperability with the `codegraph` CLI"},{"id":"p22s1","text":"[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p23s1","text":"## Why not just spawn the CLI"},{"id":"p24s1","text":"A plugin can wrap `@colbymchenry/codegraph`'s own CLI instead of reimplementing the store and indexe"},{"id":"p24s2","text":"r: `spawn` it as a subprocess, expose each of its commands as a separate tool, done in an afternoon."},{"id":"p24s3","text":" This plugin chose not to, for three concrete reasons:"},{"id":"p25s1","text":"- **No second thing to install.** Shelling out to a CLI means the host needs that binary on `PATH`, "},{"id":"p25s2","text":"at a version the plugin was actually tested against — an extra install step, and an extra way for th"},{"id":"p25s3","text":"e two to drift out of sync. `npm install` is the whole story here; the indexer and store run in-proc"},{"id":"p25s4","text":"ess.
- **Fewer tools, not more.** Every tool's schema rides along in the system prompt on every turn"},{"id":"p25s5","text":", whether or not it gets called that turn. Ten single-purpose tools (one per CLI subcommand) cost mo"},{"id":"p25s6","text":"re of that budget, every turn, than the two this plugin exposes — `codegraph`'s `operation` field is"},{"id":"p25s7","text":" a dispatch, not a compromise.
- **The parse cache is incremental; the edges are not.** "Sync only t"},{"id":"p25s8","text":"he changed files" sounds obviously faster, but the rule this graph resolves calls by — one unique na"},{"id":"p25s9","text":"me wins workspace-wide — is global: adding a symbol in file A that collides with one already indexed"},{"id":"p25s10","text":" from file B should invalidate edges that point at B, even though B never changed. A parser that rep"},{"id":"p25s11","text":"arses only the touched files *and patches in their own new edges* has no way to notice that. So this"},{"id":"p25s12","text":" plugin splits the two: each file's extraction is cached and reused (**991 ms → 45 ms** on a 337-fil"},{"id":"p25s13","text":"e workspace), while edges are rebuilt over the whole graph on every run. Reparsing everything was th"},{"id":"p25s14","text":"e wrong thing to save; re-resolving everything is cheap."},{"id":"p26s1","text":"## What this plugin adds"},{"id":"p27s1","text":"Five things you do not get from a CLI an agent shells out to:"},{"id":"p28s1","text":"1. **No second runtime.** `dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-codegraph` is the whole install — no binary on "},{"id":"p28s2","text":"`PATH`, no MCP server to wire, no version to keep in sync with the plugin.
2. **An index that starts"},{"id":"p28s3","text":" itself.** Opening a session in an unindexed workspace builds one in the background, and every chang"},{"id":"p28s4","text":"e after that is picked up by a watcher.
3. **A model that knows the state of what it is querying.** "},{"id":"p28s5","text":"Every request's prompt carries how large the index is, when it was built, and how many generated fil"},{"id":"p28s6","text":"es were skipped — for free, instead of a `status` round-trip.
4. **Entry points for a human.** `/cod"},{"id":"p28s7","text":"egraph status|index|files`, and a settings panel with a rebuild button. Neither spends a model turn."},{"id":"p28s8","text":"
5. **Re-indexes that are cheap.** A parse cache makes a repeat run 991 ms → 45 ms on a 337-file wor"},{"id":"p28s9","text":"kspace, so "just re-index before you answer" stops being an expensive habit."}],"truncated":true}
